label: 4th original token after a sequence starting e/n/j with d as 3rd token
explanation: Fires almost only in the original phase at t=3 (93% of mass; the rest at t=4, none in the copy phase). It needs the previous input to be d (98.5% of mass) and the first token to be e (66% of mass), n (24%) or j (8%), giving the prefix pattern [e|n|j] ? d -> X. It fires hardest when first_tok=e and the current input is the digit 3 (all top examples look like e ? d [3]); first_tok=n/j and other inputs give weaker activations. A small t=4 tail shows up when d is repeated or comes at position 3. It does not fire at t<3, at t>=5, in the copy phase, or after d when the first token is something else. The predicate t==3 & prev=d & first in {e,n,j} gets dev F1 0.72 and mass recall 0.90, but about a third of its matches are inactive, because the input at t=3 also matters and is not fully captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: orig0=e (+5.69), t=3 & prev_tok=d (+4.32), orig0=n (+3.72), orig0=j (+3.11), prev3_tok=n (+2.83), prev_tok=d (+2.77). Lower it: orig_idx=-1 (-2.75), in_first=0 (-1.74), prev2_tok=g (-1.53), orig1=2 (-1.34).
